Frederick stared at the glowing runes, the weight of eternity pressing against his mortal heart. The draft intensified, carrying the scent of ozone and ancient dust. He realized that immortality was not a gift, but a cage—a static existence devoid of the very urgency that gave life meaning. With a trembling hand, he did not reach for the vial of ingredients. Instead, he pulled a small, flint striker from his pocket. He struck it against the stone altar, igniting the dry parchment. As the runes curled into ash, the hidden chamber began to collapse, sealing the secret away forever. Frederick walked out into the sunlight, leaving the altar behind, finally free to live a life that would end, and therefore, truly matter.

Christopher Columbus
